Text: Ea’s blessing be with you-roo! So glad to see you-roo, adventurer!
I came out to greet you-roo as soon as I heard an adventurer was coming!
You look a bit hungry-roo. Would you like a snack? Our village is just a short walk down-roo! Let's go-roo!
[There doesn't seem to be anything particularly unusual.]

A fragment of the Tesseract Vardad spoke of.
It appears to be an ancient relic, yet it radiates no discernable power.
Let's take it for now.
[Faint traces of a massive magic circle... Nothing else seems out of the ordinary here. Wait—something’s shimmering down by the river. Let’s head over and take a closer look.]
It looks like the monsters haven't made it as far as the water cistern yet.

A signpost marking the way to the garrison.
May no adventurer lose their way…
[Without a doubt, this crest belongs to the Mercenaries.]

[Operation: Reclaim Babylon]
- Exterminate those wretched Impostors and show them who the true masters are. 
- Establish a base near Babylon and Taima Pioneer Village. Keep a close watch on them. 
- Take down Aman, that Guild Alliance Leader who treats Babylon like his personal playing. His riches and assets—they’re ours for the taking. 
 - Eliminate Muina. She’s nothing but Arhan Shah’s little pet playing Lieutenant. Once she’s gone, the Shadow Wolf Alpha will take her seat.

Just as Kamiya said, the cut is clean.
This is clearly the work of a master... what on earth happened here?
It reads: ["Bits of meat still clings to the teeth."]
[I ate the meat stuck between the teeth.]
[It reads: "Snow begins to fall upon the wasteland."]

An unfamiliar cactus I’ve never seen before...
Must be the one Yasta was talking about.
Will the monsters actually recoil from this? Hard to say, but I’ll take it for now.

Soil collected from the first site for reclamation, as Uzar mentioned.
The quality is decent, but the monsters nearby are a concern.
I should check the riverbank, too.
[This doesn't look like the cargo Nanda mentioned. Let’s keep searching for the rest of the bags.]

Black clothes and wolf tattoo.
It's the Shadow Wolf Clan, no doubt.
[Sugar Plums are fruits about the size of a fist. Children love them for their sweet flavor.]
[The Europae is a fruit tree that bears round, heavy fruit. Eating them—raw, roasted, or pickled—restores one's vitality.]
This looks like the report Baran dropped. I should return it to him.

Scattered cargo, likely from the transport unit.
I need to search the area further.

No sign of Elin. Only a small dagger and a single feather remained.
The dagger’s craftsmanship was unlike anything I’d ever seen.

Looks like a merchant guard's shield.
Has something happened to the caravan ahead?
If this is linked to the sky anomaly... I’d better move fast.

A device of unknown design.
It appears to be non-functional due to severe damage.

A faint trace remains.
Rada was right—it’s linked to an ancient civilization, but seemingly unrelated to the Rift.
Nothing more to see here. I should tell Lada what I’ve found.
No one would hide here with monsters prowling about. I'd better check the upper floors.

It looks similar to the shape Beretta described.
I should check other spots as well.
This is exactly what Beretta mentioned. Let's take it.
Looks like traces of the transport unit. I'll follow the trail of blood.
This is definitely the transport wagon, but there’s no sign of the soldiers.

Judging by the deep ruts, these must be the wagon's tracks.
They must have been chased to veer off the main road like this.
I need to pick up the pace.
Nothing seems out of the ordinary. Let's search elsewhere.
I see faint footprints. How did this happen in such a remote place? I should examine the passage.
The stash guard's body is nowhere to be found. Let's search the surroundings.
No pulse. They’re gone. I should head back to Khoon and explain the situation.
Doesn't look like the spot. Let's keep looking.
Not here either. Where could they be hiding?
The grass has been disturbed. This must be the right way....

…There is no such thing as paradise, nowhere in this world.
So please, never follow strangers,
and never eat anything just because it looks interesting...

I still remember the first time I held you in my arms, Atessa.

If I could only return to that moment, I...
I would never have brought you to the Forsaken Land.
Even if my hands had been frozen and my body had been weighted down by hunger,
I would have stayed by your side in a small tent by the oasis...

The flower Orica mentioned.
It looks as if it is shyly bowing its head.

For the expulsion of ■■ and ■■■,
for the resurgence of ■■■■■,
to claim Babylon as our own,
this grand hunt must succeed.

-■■■-

Does rotating shifts every two days even make sense?
Give us a break once every eight hours, at least.

△ Snare Merchant: Stock increased by 6 from last month (Sandmaw Tusk Necklace) 
▼ Starcluster Merchant: Stock decreased by 10 from last month (Kuduru Hind Leg) 
= Rappie Ranch: No change.

■■■ the path to ■■■ ■■■■.
Nothing serves better to cut off ■■'s reach.

On the day the ■■ rises, capture ■■■ alive and move them to ■■■.
Since I plan to report that I ■■■ ■■■■, ■■■■ ■■ ■■.

A red blossom.
This must be the herb Muina mentioned. I’d better harvest it with care.

Dive into the traces of lost time.
Right now.
From your client.

Cooking level is a bit insufficient.

“What is that even supposed to mean? Was that some kind of popular joke back then?”

Today is my day off.
I am doing absolutely, definitely, literally nothing.

A flower blooming amidst the thick brush.
I can feel its stubborn will to live.

Looks like the remains of a destroyed observatory.
I’d better recover the parts Bardad spoke of first.

Soil collected from the shade.
It’s damp to the touch, likely due to the lack of sun.

Soil collected from beneath a tree.
It's soft, thanks to plenty of sun.

A dagger engraved with the Sverd Mercenary crest.
It belonged to Mitchell, and I can still feel a faint warmth on the hilt.
I should bring this to Sharaf.

This is the flower Sharaf mentioned; it glows with a radiant light.
Let's carry this with care, with Mitchell in mind.

Nothing useful here.
I should look elsewhere.

This should be plenty of bait.
Time to head back to Zuabu.

Soil collected from the second site for reclamation, as Uzar mentioned.
The soil quality is poor, most likely a result of the incursion.
Let’s take this back to Uzar.

A haystack that looks appetizing at a glance.
Let’s bring this to Rappie right away.

Fresh footprints here.
They look to be from an adult male.
They're heading outward.

Nothing here looks like an artifact.
Let’s head further in the direction Helene mentioned.

A fragment found among the ruins with an unfamiliar script.
This could be what Helene mentioned; Let’s secure it.

Seems empty inside.
Let’s look elsewhere.

That is one massive cactus.
Enough to please Vahista, I think.
Let’s look for more cacti nearby.

Clear water that sustains the pioneer village.
Its purity is enough to satisfy even the Naruru, making it a valuable commodity.

Careful now! We should always watch out for low-temperature burns.
Let’s take them out one bottle at a time, even if Beretta is waiting.

An old barrel, very common in breweries.
Why would the Babaju Alliance hide an artifact here of all places?

Ether is entangled unnaturally.
It looks like it’s swirling violently.

I don't feel any special energy.
Let’s check further inside.

Strange vines... they stretch all the way across the wall.
I can sense a faint energy from the other side. Let’s climb up carefully.

Just act natural, as if you’re tending the crops.
No one will give you a second look.

A small, cute pouch sits here.
It hardly weighs a thing... What could be inside?

Arrange the hanging leathers properly.
No one will give you a second look.

Deep ruts in the ground.
Judging by the marks, they passed through not long ago. Let’s hurry and follow the trail.
The body of a villager lies, slain in a gruesome fashion.
Filled with illegible handwriting.

A Kiguru, a Naruru, and a human are depicted here.
There is some hastily scribbled text.
I see symbols of the Ironblood Brigade along with some unknown signs.

Found a note while searching the member’s body.
It reads: [Delay in securing supplies].
Clothes are scattered about. They appear to belong to the Kiguru Tribe.

Looks like it belongs to the Kiguru Tribe.
Let’s take one and show it to Zisen.

Still warm... must have died not long ago.
What in the world happened here?

Kuduru weapons are piled up in a mess.
Take one that looks good.

No traces of Etherium here.
Let’s look elsewhere.
Well-maintained weapons are stored, ready for immediate use.
To the right: Mountain trail.
To the left: Hesperia.

Looks a bit worn down, but surprisingly well-maintained.
I can clearly see the steady flow of people passing through the Frantia Gate in the distance.

Not a weapon or scrap of armor in sight.
With these humble buildings, it feels more like a cozy mountain lodge than an outpost.
A nice place to stay for the night...

No separate defensive structures to guard the outpost.
When you see it like this, Hesperia feels like a truly livable neighborhood...

A crumpled map from Ophelia.
It appears to depict the whole of Pulsing Ridge.
Cryptic symbols are written all over it.

Only the last beacon left.
Finish this quickly and head back to Jean.

No issues with the beacon.
Moving on to the next one.

No need to retrieve the beacon yet.
I should let Jean know.

With this weight, even the Kuduru will struggle.
Let’s pack the rest of the boxes with stones, just as Thierry planned.

A flower crown woven with care for Dunie.
I can almost picture Dunie’s smiling face.
The ■ when ■■■ is ■■, and ■■ is ■■ not far off.

Left behind for the White Lion, forever a step behind.
The wolf’s fangs are still intact.
The cargo is filled with stones instead of Etherium.

The blood has oxidized to a brown hue.
Looks like quite some time has passed since the stains were left.

A letter addressed to the Merchants Guild.
Stained with blood in places,
the sender's name is scrawled in haste: North Sea Light.

A receipt signed by the North Sea Light, along with some Etherium.
It even has some Etherium candies mixed in.

A letter is visible through the torn clothes.
It bears the seal of the manor.
Lying collapsed while clutching an Etherium candy.
A miner, clad in the garb of the Shadow Wolf Clan, lies collapsed.

Etherium candies in the brush.
They look exactly like the ones distributed by the Paradise Advent.
Looks like a fake Etherium candy, crafted by the Naruru from monster dung and teeth.
A mix of real and fake Etherium candies here.

Surprisingly well-made for a rush job.
Definitely enough to fool the Wolf Clan.

A flower blooming upon the rock. I can feel its stubborn will to live.
I should deliver this to Yasta.
The water condition... it’s not as bad as I’d feared.

A stone block needed to carve a false relic.
I should take this to Orha.
A potion that looks like it could be used as an antidote.

Not a human head—it’s an otter's.
No, not an otter, it’s a Naruru!
Wait, that back looks familiar... it's Azid’s!

Blood is splattered everywhere.
Someone must be critically wounded...
They won’t have made it far, losing this much blood.
Whose trail is this?

The energy is even more potent than at the entrance.
It’s just like those Etherium candies...
Could this ore be yet another trace of the Paradise Advent?

The smell is unbelievable, beyond imagination.
They make Babaju with this?
But the liquor didn't smell anything like it...

The smell is unbelievable, beyond imagination.
No, I feel a hint of intoxication... My head is spinning…
The world is turning…

It stinks, though not as bad as fermenting Baba.
Since these are the droppings of an evolved species, the shape is... well, perfect.

How do they even brew this into medicine?
No one could stomach this if they knew what it was made of—no matter how good it is for them.

The gatherers might not have feared the mutant animals.
It’s possible they were terrified of this instead… It’s a truly grueling task.
Is this... a letter?
It's a statue that looks exactly like the Naruru.

To prevent the monsters from swallowing it,
I retrieved the Aetherium.
There are only stones in the pouch.
It's a sturdy-looking herb.

It's a fresh-looking herb.
I think I’ve gathered enough... just a bit more to be sure.

I think this should be enough.
Time to head back to Beretta.

Just as Beretta taught me...
I've finely minced the herbs and blended them with the potion.
It has a color similar to Aetherium.

A possession of the Prophet.
It looks like a very thick tome.

No stairs or ropes in sight.
One wrong step and I'll twist an ankle.
This crossing definitely wasn't built with convenience in mind.

A thick stalagmite resembles a wooden pillar.
Water bottles, traps, and crates are scattered around its base.
Could this have served as a food storehouse?

The timber is neatly stacked.
I’ve never heard of monsters building fires,
so the people who lived here must have left it behind.

A small watchtower, low enough to scale without a ladder.
Tattered cloth and leather hang from its frame.
If you don’t toss and turn too much, it might just pass for a bed.

Traces of freshly turned soil.
It appears someone dug deep to plant seeds here.

A tiny sprout has emerged.
Though it’s just a seedling, the tips are already starting to yellow…

A small animal—maybe a rabbit or a squirrel—has dug up the soil.
No leaves remain; only thin, exposed roots are left behind.
A map showing the area around the Encampment.

This must be the herb Beretta mentioned.
Better take this carefully.
Wood that looks suitable for physical training.
It looks sturdy. Should make for a decent barricade.
At this size and weight, it should fit in the chest just fine.

The craftsmanship appears far more sophisticated than anything from the Shadow Wolf Clan
or the Kiguru Tribe.
A robe from a Paradise Advent follower. Looks like it’s seen years of wear.

A description of the Paradise Advent's holy place.
The text is smudged, leaving the details illegible.
Nothing here. I’ll have to look elsewhere.

A Tesseract Fragment, the kind found where an incursion occurred.
It looks similar to those used by the Shadow Wolf Clan.

Footprints in the grass.
It looks like someone passed through here.

The footprints are a jumbled mess.
They must belong to a group of people.
I wish the manual had clearer instructions on how to use this.
A few more chairs and some food would make this place perfect.

Water flows toward the hot springs.
The stream looks refreshing as it cascades.

The waterfall roars.
Its waters are incredibly clear.

Looks scorching hot.
I’m not sure what this is, but the scent is piercing—almost stinging my nose.

This must be the Kuduru’s doing.
It’s far too sloppy to be the work of soldiers.
Supplies, likely hauled in from the outpost.
Packed to the brim with Etherium candies.

Supply boxes.
No sign of Etherium candies in these.
Searched the belongings and found an Etherium candy.

A massive stash of Etherium candies.
Let’s take every last one.

More Etherium candies piled up here.
Better not drop a single one.
Rare herbs that thrive even in bitter cold.
Cleared the snow, but there’s nothing underneath.

It looks like the seal Gale used.
I’d better keep it safe and not lose it.
Steady breathing. Appears to be in a deep sleep.
I didn't expect to see this here. It seems to hold even more water than the ones in the wasteland.
A large, sturdy Starfish Flower. Davin from Taima Pioneer Village would surely prize this.

For Gilbert...
The banquet is set.

A monster bounty from Ranon.
Bounties are listed under portraits of menacing creatures.
Beasts, insects, and plants…
Go ahead and pick the most formidable-looking of the lot.

<Food Storage – No Entry>
- Manager is temporarily absent. Contact the General Store for emergency grain supplies.

<Hunting Grounds Cleaning Schedule Change>
- The Southern Hunting Grounds will not be 'cleared' until the designated hunter returns.
- Non-hunters are advised to take an alternate path.

No sign of anything near the warp anchors.
Let’s search again from a spot with a clear view of the village.

I hear whispering... Who is it?
I need to get closer for a better look.

No sign of anything resembling a horn, no matter how thoroughly I search.
If it’s truly something a dragon would covet, it must be hidden deeper within.
Nothing special across the water. Focus the search further inside.

Resonance of vitality from the lake.
It is nearly identical to what we discovered with Beretta,
yet it feels as though impurities have bled into it.

A formless mass that orbited the top floor of Giant’s Tower.
The team on-site refers to it as ‘floating matter’ as they continue their investigation.
I can feel a faint Ether pulse sparking from it.

An offering—no, a proper meal for Khoon’s hunting hawk.
Someone took great care not to singe it.
No bird of prey could possibly turn this down.

The communal area of the Nameless Village.
Surprisingly, the search turned up absolutely nothing out of the ordinary.
Only common grains and vegetables are neatly arranged—
and even those are so scarce that you couldn’t find a single scrap to scavenge, tainted or otherwise.

A well that draws clean groundwater.
Its smell and taste seem perfectly fine.

It is written in neat handwriting, though it conveys a slight sense of tension.
At the end, it reads “Hekima, Liberator of Knowledge.”

- Likely location is Tan, the former territory of Karadia.
- Will investigate whether the power source has been disguised as a special artifact and released to the public.

... Rappie is nowhere to be seen.
Doesn't look like the spot. Let's keep looking.

<Volunteers Wanted: 'Nameless Village' Dispatch>
- Seeking volunteers to search for the missing.
- Packed lunches provided (no additional meal allowance).
- We welcome any descendant of Tan who is willing to lend a hand!

An herb commonly used for disinfection and stopping bleeding.
Considering Seta's physique, you need to pack plenty.

...Don't tell me they actually ate stones out of starvation?
There must be another use for this.

Tree barks are edible if dried well and smoothed out.
Though it can be brewed in drinking water as medicine,
but it still has a taste you wouldn't want in your mouth.

At least these weeds look like they can be used as ingredients.
There might be poisonous plants mixed in...

Seeds of the Balsam flower, which grows well in moist soil.
Known to be used for dyeing and as an effective medicine.

Catnip planted here and there by Bau.
Let's gather a little more before setting out.

What is it about this grass
that makes cats go so crazy...?

This should be enough.
Let's return to Bau.

The water looks clear, but leaves a bitter taste on the tip of the tongue.
Maybe we should do something about the water quality here.

The bark of the tree trunk is dry and crumbly.
Peeling it off reveals white ants moving in a line.
This tree is already suffering!

It looks adequately moist and healthy at a glance, but
judging from the faded color at leaf tips, it’s not getting enough nutrients.

A pile of tournament invitations.
It would take quite a while to sign them all...
My hand already feels sore just thinking about it.

I found an object with a faint trace of Aether, but it briefly glowed before disappearing.
It quickly lost its color, turning into an ordinary gray stone.
It is hard to even consider it an artifact.

There is a Tesseract replica among the jumbled junk.
I heard the Kuduru tribe often steals human belongings...
Could it have belonged to someone who did not know its purpose?

Karugura's Factor.
As I place it into the Replica Seed, a faint light flickers.

Karugura's Factor.
I placed it into the Replica Seed, but there is no change.
I believe I followed Bailey's instructions, so this is strange.

Karugura's Factor.
I placed it into the Replica Seed, but there is no change.
I believe I followed Bailey's instructions, so this is strange.

A doll modeled after the Naruru tribe.
It looks cozy and soft.
It feels completely out of place here.

Tagar's Factor.
As I place it into the Replica Seed, a faint light flickers.

Tagar's Factor.
As I place it into the Replica Seed, it emits an intense light.

An herb to be used as an ingredient for Rappie's snacks.
Looks to be in good condition.
I think this should be enough.
Hopefully, the wild Rappie will react well to this...

The Token of Romance that Uran mentioned.
It stands tall and blooms even on the withered hill.

The Form Recording Device isn't working.
It seems to be broken.

Check the Form Recording Device under the Ancient Tree Bower.

P.S. Things were too urgent to put it in the safe.
I left a potion instead. Apply it to the mercenary group's mark, then shine a light on it.
There is nothing in the rock crevice.
There is no trace of the Form Recording Device among the grass either.
It is an intact Form Recording Device.
It contains leftover meat and what looks like a tribute from the Naruru tribe.
It contains a broken Form Recording Device.
It is a parchment bearing the mark of the Polaris Clan.
These are the bones of the people who were dragged to the sanctuary.
It appears the candle was blown out not too long ago.
Given the clear bloodstains, it seems to have been used recently.
There are bloodstained marks left behind.

Something has been dropped near the candle.
… It looks like the bandana Libby always wore.

The cluster of light that Hekima calls “my remnant.”
It's fragmented as if a rift has formed in space.

It has a deeper color than they appeared from the outside.
For some reason, I feel strangely drawn to it.
Did a large bird drop this feather? It doesn’t look like any species I’ve seen in Elsetia.
Looking closer, it has a familiar shape. It almost looks as if it once belonged to a person...

A large white feather, as big as an adult's palm.
Strangely, the energy covering the “Labyrinth” emanates from this feather.
It might be related to the ancient empire.

I searched thoroughly, but found nothing.
It looked like a good place to hide things...

Could this be written in the Talim script the Liberators mentioned?
I can’t even understand the title.

I could read it naturally in the ruins...
But now it just looks like drawings.
I discovered an intact Form Recording Device.

It is the dagger I saw when I met Elin. No way... 
Let's head down quickly.

The herb illustrated in the recipe Weifel mentioned.
Better take this carefully.

The pile of books the old man gestured toward with a nod.
Some are so faded from cover to page that the text is barely legible.
<The Three Little Bisons>, <The Rappia Piper>...
Yet among them... not a single book is about the 'Sentinel of the Deep Woods'!

In an instant, a flash! Light reflected from the dusty mound of dirt.
I carefully dug out that spot, but what appeared was... a worn piece of brass armor.

As I rummaged through the gaps in the stone pillars, my hand caught on a small, round object.
As I rubbed the grimy surface clean... a gold coin appeared!

There is no heartbeat, not even a faint breath to be heard.
Without the slightest stir... it's like looking at an exquisite doll.

It’s similar to what I checked with Beretta back at the ridges.
Vitality, a chilly cold, distortion, and a violent vortex... I can feel them all.

I've seen objects that anchor Aether before,
But this is my first time seeing one that collects it all in one place...
It's reliable enough to use, I suppose?

A flower blooming in the middle of a meadow.
I think Etana would love this.

A small flower blooming beneath a tree.
This would also be a nice addition.

A flower nearly hidden against a rock.
Its colors are truly striking.

A modified phase shift device made by Asli.
It is shattered beyond repair.

It is a fresh bloodstain.
It might be Asli's, so we need to find her quickly.
I never expected to find an Aether entanglement in a place like this...
Perhaps because these are ancient ruins, they are easier to find.

A broken object that appears ancient is tangled with light.
It looks dangerous. I had better take it with me.

Aether flowing from a suspicious mage.
It could be dangerous, so I should collect it carefully.

Aether flowing from a suspicious mage.
 It looks unusually complex and tangled.

A storage box surrounded by faint Aether.
It seems to have protective measures to prevent accidents.
The object inside... looks incredibly bizarre!

I sense a higher density than the rift I saw earlier.
 It does not look special on the surface,
but it feels strangely massive...

Just as Adel said, this does not look like a wound caused in ordinary combat.
The flesh is torn and ragged, as if strong jaws tore into the flesh...
I see a corpse in the distance missing half its torso, likely bearing the same gruesome marks.

I can’t tell whether the giant has already escaped.
I should look for footprints just in case...
Wait, is this a letter?

I've finished filling out Evrin's questionnaire.
This should be enough, right...?

Nothing out of the ordinary, aside from the large bite marks.
I should at least collect a blood sample, since Monica has me on this job.

The rapid blinking light suggests an artifact is nearby.
And the detector's needle... is pointing south.

Notice to the denizens of the Forsaken Land.

To minimize casualties caused by a 'Giant Humanoid' creature,
an emergency evacuation order is hereby issued.

Babylon classifies this situation as an anomaly triggered by an artifact and is making every effort to recover it.

- Formation of conduits between Elsetia and the unstable reaches of space and time.
- Materialization of entities mimicking those from the connected realms.

Unidentified entities may emerge from these conduits. All must strictly adhere to the evacuation order.

Traces left where the Giant disappeared.
Looks like gray smoke.
It would feel unpleasant if it got on you.

Traces left where the Intelligent Giant disappeared.
Seems darker than before.

Liquid similar to what was found earlier.
The more you look at it, the more unpleasant it feels.
Human footprints are mixed chaotically.
It contains military supplies to be sent to the Ashientet Governor-General's Office.
It looks like they used up all the medicine they prepared.
It appears they use the fallen leaves as firewood.
It contains grains grown through the hard work of farmers.
They say your wish will come true if you drink water from this fountain.
Bowls with stunning patterns. It is said an artisan handcrafted after single one.
These fruits were grown under the scorching sun of the Scything Barrens.
Weapons containing Istarium, found only in the Forsaken Land.
A box cherished by Imad, the Stash manager. What could be inside?
A jar holding items supposedly shown only to special guests. It looks like they are all sold out today.
I came here expecting free liquor but left empty-handed.
It is the perfect place to hide from the sun and the soldiers' gaze.
A stone statue modeled after the great hero of Asientet.

A hand-stitched cushion.
The patterns are supposedly decided on a whim.
For some reason, I feel like I will be visiting this place often.
A delicious aroma is coming from the boiling pot.
It looks like it was used to carry grain.
A box with unknown contents. It could be dangerous, so let's leave it alone.
Judging by the nearby jars, sacks, and small carpets, these boxes were likely left behind by merchants.
It looks like the perfect place to hide from the Incursion.
A vantage point overlooking the entire Bardad Expedition Garrison.
A snack favored by the expedition members. They reportedly prefer steamed potatoes over baked ones.
Boxes filled with goods stolen by the Kuduru tribe. Getting too curious might start a fight with them.
It appears to be a peddler's wagon. It looks like it broke down recently.
It appears someone left some liquor behind. I am thirsty, so I’ll drink it now.
These are grains brought in from Babylon. They are food supplies for the residents of the Gale Ruins Encampment.
The corpse of a recently deceased Sandmaw. Who could have killed it?
The corpse still feels warm. There are marks indicating it was pierced by something sharp.
It seems to have been struck down in a single blow by great force. Was it a mage? Or a warrior..?
With so many fruits and grains here, no one would notice if some went missing.

A box containing handcrafted goods by the Naruru tribe.
Naruru merchants transport them directly all the way to Babylon.
Hay gathered for the priest's prayers to the god Ea.
The piled-up hay is either delivered to the priest or used as feed for the Rappies.
Ingredients for dried salmon noodles, a Naruru specialty.
A smoothie made by grinding dried salmon and assorted vegetables together. It provides a hearty meal for the Naruru.
A giant cactus with blooming red flowers. The red petals are used as dye or festival decorations for the Naruru.
A carriage driven by the Naruru. It contains boxes of fish, grains, and crafts to be taken to Babylon.
A barrel filled with strong liquor made from Baba. It seems no one remembers how many years it has been aging.
The remnants of a facility where the ancient empire once drilled and refined Aether.
The remnants of a facility where the ancient empire once drilled and refined Aether. Ancient characters are engraved on it.
A manger filled with fresh hay that Rappies like. The Naruru fill it with fresh hay daily.
The Naruru soak Baba, the ingredient for their liquor, in water to remove its toxins.
A Baba field carefully cultivated by the Naruru. Most of the produced Baba is used to brew liquor.
Well-trimmed Baba. To become a master brewer, one must know how to prepare Baba properly.
Freshly harvested Baba. It must be soaked in water to remove toxins and prepared before it can be used.
A tree with large and sturdy roots. You can cross to the other side via a bridge built above the tree.

The ruling class of the Ancient Empire possessed innate abilities.
 
◈ Innate Abilities ◈
Innate abilities refer to the inherent supernatural powers possessed by living beings. While most species manifest a specific, uniform type of power, human abilities are remarkably diverse in both form and potency. This difference is often characterized as "talent."
 
Innate abilities are primarily hereditary, though there are exceptions. Notable exceptions occur. Children may manifest abilities despite having non-gifted parents, and conversely, the offspring of powerful users may be born without any innate power at all.
 
Because the possession and mastery of innate abilities naturally divided society into the ruling and ruled classes, the possession of an inherited innate ability was an important topic among the imperial family and nobles. There are even records of some nobles killing or abandoning children who lacked innate abilities.
